Oct 15, 2026 • Less than a minute read

Invited commentary on Lancet Digital Health *From reactive diagnosis to proactive triage - connecting the dots at labour onset*. [DOI:10.1016/j.landig.2026.101066](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landig.2026.101066).

Our invited Comment, “From reactive diagnosis to proactive triage - connecting the dots at labour onset”, is now published online in The Lancet Digital Health. It accompanies Bozhilova and colleagues’ Fit4Labour study, a prognostic model that uses the first 20 minutes of computerised CTG and routine clinical risk factors to flag severe fetal compromise at the start of labour.

We argue that the field needs to shift from diagnosing damage, often too late to change outcomes, to identifying at-risk fetuses early enough to prevent injury. It is identifying at-risk fetuses early enough to prevent injury. We see Fit4Labour as one layer of a broader, multimodal risk picture that would add three data streams developed largely in isolation - linked longitudinal health records, maternal oral health and the oral microbiome, and continuous wearable monitoring. We also highlight the AI challenges in fusing these streams - knowing when a model is extrapolating reliably, and whether a signal is genuinely biological or just a proxy for factors such as smoking and deprivation.

Read it at [DOI:10.1016/j.landig.2026.101066](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.landig.2026.101066).

Wu, Honghan, and Zhi Wang. “From reactive diagnosis to proactive triage: connecting the dots at labour onset.” The Lancet Digital Health (2026). DOI:10.1016/j.landig.2026.101066.
